title: Romantic Sunset
text:
How beautiful the sun appears when freshly it rises,

Giving good morning as in an explosion

—Happy the one who can, pierced through by love,

Greet the setting sun, more glorious than a dream.


I remember it!... I have seen everything, flower, furrow, fountain,

Fall beneath its gaze like a living heart...

—Quickly, quickly, it is late, let us go to the horizon

To catch at least some oblique ray.


But in vain I pursue the God who withdraws;

Irresistible Night establishes its empire,

Black, damp, fatal, broken by shivers;


A smell of tombs floats in the darkness,

And my fearful foot brushes, beside the marsh,

Unexpected toads and frozen slugs.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the poem's shift from romantic sunset pursuit into marsh, tomb-smell, and cold creatures.

title: Destruction
text:
Beside me without cease the Demon stirs;

Around me he floats like an impalpable air;

I swallow him and feel how he burns my lungs,

Filling them with guilty and infinite desire.


Sometimes, for he knows of my love for Art,

He takes on the appearance of the most seductive woman,

And, resorting to specious flatterer's pretexts,

Accustoms my lips to depraved filters.


Thus he carries me far from the gaze of God,

Panting and undone by fatigue, to the center

Of the deep and lonely plains of Boredom,


And casts before my eyes, filled with confusion,

Stained garments and half-open wounds,

And the bloody apparatus that lives in Destruction!
editorial_note: The translation preserves the demon as temptation, artistic seduction, boredom, and visible machinery of destruction.

title: The Two Good Sisters
text:
Debauchery and Death are two good girls,

Lavish with their kisses and rich in health,

Whose virginal flank, covered by rags,

Under eternal sowing never bore fruit.


To the sinister poet, blemish of families,

Favorite of hell, unpaid courtier,

Within their recesses, tomb and brothel show

A bed that anxiety never frequented,


And coffin and alcove, in fertile blasphemies,

By turns offer us, like good sisters,

Frightful pleasures and horrendous sweetnesses.


Filthy License, when at last will you bury me?

When will you come, Death, her fascinating rival,

To graft your cypresses onto her infected myrtles?
editorial_note: The translation keeps the blasphemous pairing of debauchery and death as sisterly consolations.

title: When at the Bottom You Sleep, My Dark Beauty
text:
When at the bottom you sleep, my dark beauty,

Of a vault worked in dark marble,

And you have no more for chamber and dwelling

Than a rain-soaked cave and a bony grave;


When the earth presses on your lazy flesh

And your flanks that idleness has charmingly polished,

And there is neither love nor heartbeat in your heart,

Nor can your feet go after anything,


The tomb, confidant of my infinite dream,

On those nights from which sleep is banished

—the tomb and the poet are sister and brother—


Will say to you: "Courtesan of uncertain charms,

What good is it now to have ignored the dead?"

Like remorse the worm will gnaw you.
editorial_note: The translation preserves the address to the dead beloved and the tomb's retaliatory speech.

title: Recollection
text:
Be wise, my Sorrow, and remain calm.

You were demanding Night; it descends now, here it is:

A dark atmosphere wraps the city,

Bringing peace to some and unease to most.


While the great mass of vile mortals,

Under Pleasure's whip, that impassive executioner,

Harvests disappointments at the servile feast,

Offer me your hand, my Sorrow, come here,


Far from them. Look at the years gone by swaying,

In ridiculous garments, upon the balustrades

Of heaven; mocking nostalgia already rises from the waters;


The dying sun rests beneath an arch,

And, like an enormous belated shroud, toward the East,

Listen, dear one, listen how Night advances.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the intimate address to Sorrow and the theatrical arrival of Night over the city.
